reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-4 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the picture graph. How many are in dogs?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: 4 of the 7 samples (seeds 44, 45, 47, 48) are bare 3-digit number comparisons ('Which is greater: 307 or 270?') with no pictograph, table, or dataset in sight, so they do not exercise 'interpret data in tabular form and in a pictograph' at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only seeds 42 and 46 ('Look at the picture graph. How many are in dogs?') actually reference a pictograph; the remaining majority of the sampled seeds are generic magnitude-comparison items with numbers up to 930 unrelated to any dataset.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Both the pictograph-reading stems and the numeric comparison stems are short single-clause sentences appropriate for grade-2 quarter-3 reading level.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The registered dnas list 'comparing_ordering' alongside 'pictographs', and the observed output shows that DNA is generating off-topic 3-digit magnitude comparisons instead of pictograph-derived comparisons (e.g. 'which category has more'), so the variant pool leaks unrelated content.

competency_alignment.rationale: 'Which is greater: 92 or 930?' tests raw numeral comparison, a skill from the number-and-algebra strand, not 'interpret data in tabular form and in a pictograph' which is the explicit wording of this dp-branch competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Where a pictograph is actually shown the answer options (A/B/C) and where comparisons are numeric, the values (up to 930) are consistent with grade-2 3-digit number familiarity, so scale itself is not the problem here.
